amendment_reason: Pre-protected source audit found that D1 _serialize_typed does not encode list indices in paths. Ordered list semantics, including directed dependency pairs [0,1] versus [1,0], are therefore carried partly by token sequence order. The V1/V1.1 requirement of arbitrary token-order permutation invariance would destroy semantic information and the initial multiset comparator could falsely merge reversed dependencies.
scientific_change: F1 must preserve the ordered token subsequence within each side/coordinate block. It may be invariant to global reordering of whole coordinate blocks because coordinate paths identify those blocks. All D1 data, labels, splits, historical arms, model grid, F1/F2 thresholds, and protected test remain unchanged.
removed_hostile_requirement: arbitrary token order permutation does not change F1 features
replacement_hostile_requirements: reordering whole side/coordinate blocks while preserving within-block token order leaves F1 features unchanged
reversing the ordered children of a directed dependency tuple changes the dependencies equality feature
F2 equals the historical exact typed comparator on train+dev before protected S3 execution
interpretation: The canonical serialization is lossless only when its order semantics are respected.
S3 tests generic paired-coordinate access over the existing serialization; it does not claim that sequence order is irrelevant.
Any future order-invariant representation must first make ordered child positions explicit, e.g. indexed paths, tuples, pointers, or another reversible encoding.
outcome_policy: No S3 protected test access before V1.2 hostile tests and implementation are committed and the train+dev-only exact-equivalence gate is green.
